content:
sam (eng): kicking off — drop any leftover pricing/packaging/quotas questions from today's all-hands. leadership on standby: @maia, @chris, @heather.
maia (product): thanks — prefer short threads so we can triage quickly. if you need a follow-up, we'll create a ticket.
anya (support): quick question: do trial credits expire automatically when you hit billing? we had a customer confused today.
heather (finance): for self-serve trials purchased via the console: trial credits expire 180 days after grant unless converted to a paid plan. we're updating the FAQ to be explicit. :memo:
sam (eng): clarifying: if a customer upgrades to paid before 180d, do unused credits carry over?
heather (finance): yes — unused trial credits convert into account credits that decay on the same 180d schedule from original grant. enterprise prepay contracts are separate (we handle on a case-by-case basis).
chris (CEO): long-term we're exploring a rollover product, but it's not in the near roadmap because it changes revenue recognition and unit economics.
anya (support): another: what happens to per-route quotas when we do a canary rollout? e.g., smaller model for fallbacks but same route.
maia (product): good one. behavior today: quotas are evaluated per API key + route. during canaries we respect the route config. if fallback triggers a different route/model, that call is charged against the fallback route quota. we have a ticket to show a composite view in Console.
sam (eng): any hard limits for dev orgs? a partner hit 120 requests/s and got 429s even though they were under token quota.
maia (product): dev orgs have burst protection but we enforce short-term RPS caps to protect the shared pool. token quotas are monthly; RPS is plumbed separately. for predictable throughput use Dedicated.
ops-bot: deploy event: dedicated/region-fallback policy updated 09:41 — no customer-facing changes.
chris (CEO): to add: Dedicated is the recommendation for production with steady >50 RPS sustained. that guidance is in the runbook.
anya (support): customer also asked about the `X-RateLimit-Reset` header showing a timestamp in the past — was that a bug?
maia (product): that was a bug we fixed yesterday; header displayed server local time instead of epoch seconds UTC. fix deployed; existing SDKs will ignore the header safely.
sam (eng): thanks. last product question: do credits apply to embeddings differently? we have latency-sensitive customers asking to segregate embedding usage for cost accounting.
heather (finance): embeddings and generations are charged by unit (embedding unit vs token unit) per the pricing page. we can create dedicated billing buckets for large customers to separate embedding spend — need support ticket and billing enablement.
maia (product): adding that we're launching tag-based usage labels in Console next quarter so teams can split usage by project/route in the UI.
anya (support): follow-up: are there exemptions for rate limits for partners during migration windows (e.g., data migration)?
heather (finance): short answer: we can grant temporary increased quotas but it requires a written request and a formal temporary contract amendment for higher committed capacity or grace credits. reach out to partnerships@sales.
chris (CEO): operational principle: we want predictable behavior. if you need burst capacity that changes traffic shape, tell us ahead of migration and we'll scope a plan.
sam (eng): can we get a one-liner we can paste in support replies about how rate limits, quotas, and credits interact?
maia (product): sure — paste: `Rate limits (RPS) protect live serving and are enforced per-key; quotas (monthly units/credits) track spend and do not prevent short bursts unless RPS caps are hit; credits offset charges but follow the same expiry rules. For production-scale steady throughput use Dedicated or request quota increases through support.`
anya (support): perfect — will paste and link to runbooks.
maia (product): action: I'll file a Console feature request for composite quota views and tag-based labeling.
heather (finance): action: I'll update the FAQ language about credit expiry and conversion to paid accounts.
chris (CEO): action: we'll evaluate feasibility of a controlled rollover pilot later this year.
sam (eng): thanks everyone. if you raised a private case we'll follow up there. closing the thread in 24h unless new Qs. :wave:
